messages:
lena: Support escalated from AcmeFinance - multiple 504s over the last 20m. They report intermittent timeouts against hosted inference endpoints. Sample request IDs: req_8a3f, req_8a7b. Filing here to triage, @oncall

support-bot: New ticket created: SF-5982 (AcmeFinance) — Severity: high. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/SF-5982 :rotating_light:

jamie: looking now. I can see p95 backend latency spikes coincident with the customer's 504s, lots of gateway 502/504 in the same time window.

morgan: pulling ingress/gateway metrics — request_queue_depth for hosted-gateway jumped to ~4096 (hitting our configured hard limit) at 17:24 UTC. continuous-batcher backlog spiked, KV cache eviction rate jumped 10x.

phil: can you paste the relevant logs/traces from the gateways and batchers?

morgan: logs snippet:```[2026-03-16T17:23:58Z] gateway: tenant=acme req=req_8a3f enqueue_depth=4092 status=queued
[2026-03-16T17:24:01Z] batcher: tenant=acme batch_wait_ms=12000 batches_queued=24 kv_cache_evictions=183
[2026-03-16T17:24:32Z] gateway: tenant=acme req=req_8a7b timeout=30000 outcome=504
[2026-03-16T17:24:40Z] runtime: kv_miss_hot_keys=54 stall_ms=2300
```

sara: customer provided a short repro:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1200}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` they get 504 after ~30s consistently during the spike.

jamie: initial hypothesis: tenant-specific burst of long-gen requests created a continuous-batcher backlog. The batcher held open long-running batches, which combined with a KV-cache miss storm caused dequeue delays and pushed the gateway queue to its limit. Result: gateway started rejecting/timeouting tail requests.

lena: we need an immediate mitigation for the customer while we investigate root cause. Options: increase per-tenant queue limit, enable a model fallback to a smaller/quantized variant, or add burst capacity. Thoughts?

phil: I can push a quick config to raise the hosted-gateway per-tenant queue_limit for acme from 4096 -> 8192 and add a route-level fallback to gpt-medium-quant for long generations. Will coordinate with infra.

infra-bot: config rollout started: set tenant.acme.queue_limit=8192 on gateways 3/3 -> OK. Applying route fallback to gpt-medium-quant -> OK.

morgan: metrics after change: queue_depth dropped from 4096 -> ~1200 in ~90s, continuous-batcher backlog reduced, KV evictions down by 78%. First post-change request returned 200.

sara: customer confirmed they saw a dramatic drop in 504s in the last 5m but still reporting p95 ~2.8s on some long generations (expected due to model size). They asked for timeline on permanent fix.

jamie: follow-ups (root cause): the continuous-batcher logic allowed long-wait batches for tenants with bursty, long-gen traffic while our KV-sharding/hot-key protection didn't throttle the hot prefixes. Action items: (1) add tenant-protected batch-time cap, (2) add adaptive fallback when queue depth > 70%, (3) harden KV hot-key eviction protection and shard hot prefixes.

lena: owners: postmortem write-up = jamie, infra config hardening + rollout = phil, customer follow-up and status updates = sara. I'll draft the customer-facing note and mark SF-5982 with the mitigation.

phil: proposed quick patch (candidate): reduce batcher.batch_wait_threshold_ms from 12000 -> 6000 for tenant buckets and implement adaptive-batching rollback when tenant_queue_util > 0.7. Will open PR and smoke test on staging.

morgan: attaching traces for deeper analysis: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abc123 and short flamegraph showing batcher stall at https://perf.redwood.ai/flame/acme-20260316

support-bot: Logged follow-ups in SF-5982: mitigation applied, postmortem owner assigned, customer notified. Leaving ticket open for validation.

lena: thanks team — mitigation helped, customer is less impacted. If recurrence happens, escalate to eng-runtime and we may need a global change to batcher heuristics. For now marking this incident thread for tracking and follow-up. :white_check_mark:
